Round 9 delivered the most significant theoretical progress of the session: the Prover completed Cases 1 and 2 of the H⊔H r-EKR theorem, giving the first genuinely proved cases of the split-type decomposition. Case 1 (F₀ ≠ ∅, some sets lie entirely in H₂): F₀ is an intersecting r-family in H₂, so IH(H,r) gives a star at u∈H₂. Any S∈F_k (k≥1) must intersect every T∈F₀; since S₁⊆H₁ and T⊆H₂ are disjoint as vertex sets, S₂∩T≠∅ for all T∈star_u, forcing u∈S₂. Hence u appears in every set of F, giving F⊆star_u(G). Case 2 is symmetric. These cases are complete proofs, not sketches. Case 3 (all splits genuinely mixed, 1≤k≤r-1) remains: for r=2 it reduces to the already-proved cross-pair argument; for r≥3, the sub-case where all H₁-projections align at a common vertex is also settled, but the mixed-alignment sub-case needs further work.

The Checker reviewed the two unchecked items from Round 8. PA-DD93B0 (split-type decomposition) was confirmed flawed: the per-split bound is correct but the consolidation 'WLOG by symmetry' is unjustified — different splits could have different star centres v₁, v₂,..., and summing their bounds does not yield a single Q_v. The Checker identified the precise fix direction: use cross-split intersections to force a common centre. DA-E0BC38 was again reclassified as supporting evidence (all attacks confirmed HT).

The Experimenter ran key computational verifications. The initial Bron-Kerbosch implementation had a bug (self-loops in the intersection graph — adj[i][i]=True), which was corrected. A crucial correction: μ(Dodecahedron)=6 (not 5 as previously claimed), witness {0,2,8,12,15,17}. Since the Dodecahedron is vertex-transitive, HT holds trivially for it.

The Prover closed Case 3 via a size-comparison argument: any all-mixed intersecting r-family F lies in Σ_{k=1}^{r-1} |I^k_v(H)|·|I^{r-k}(H)|, strictly missing the k=r term |I^r_v(H)|>0 (since μ(H)≥r), so F is sub-maximal. This, combined with Cases 1 and 2, proves H⊔H is r-EKR for 1≤r≤μ(H⊔H)/2. The Disprover confirmed the corrected Q_v formula (k starts at 1, not 0) and verified the gap computationally on 2P₄ and 2C₉. The Searcher ran BK on Petersen⊔C₉ for r=1,2,3, confirming max_fam=max_star=100 at r=3. The Experimenter proved C₅⊔C₇ is strictly 2-EKR.

round_summaries.narrative: Round 11 sharpens the remaining gap in the H+H r-EKR proof. The Checker correctly identified that PA-614F19 (Case 3) has a logical gap: bounding F-sets through a single vertex v does not bound |F| when F lacks a common vertex. However, combining the per-split bound (PA-DD93B0) with the all-mixed constraint gives |F| <= Sum_{k=1}^{r-1} max_v |I^k_v(H)| * |I^{r-k}(H)|. The Prover showed this sum is < max star iff DELTA < |I^r_{v**}|, where DELTA measures how much the per-split maxima using different vertices exceed v**'s contributions. For vertex-transitive H, DELTA=0 identically (proved). Computationally, DELTA < |I^r_{v**}| holds for all tested H (P5, C9). H+H r-EKR is now fully proved for vertex-transitive H; the general case reduces to the single inequality DELTA < |I^r_{v**}|.

round_summaries.narrative:
Round 14 delivers the first concrete progress on Case 3 for non-vertex-transitive H. The Leaf Domination Theorem (PA-B9F3A1) proves: for any tree T, every leaf u dominates every non-leaf v in the sense |I^k_u(T)| ≥ |I^k_v(T)| for ALL k, via the clean injection σ: S ↦ (S\{v})∪{u}. This immediately implies v** is a leaf for trees, and if additionally the same leaf wins all per-k maxima (Star Alignment for Trees, SP-5C3F91), then DELTA=0 and Case 3 is closed for H=T. Computational data (34 pairs, all DELTA=0) strongly supports this. The remaining open sub-claim is Arm-Length Monotonicity (SP-D1E8B2): the leaf on the longest arm dominates all other leaves for all k simultaneously. The DA checker confirms no counterexample to DELTA<|I^r_{v**}| exists for n≤11.

Round 14 achieves a major analytical breakthrough: LHS ≤ max_star for r=3 is PROVED analytically from the definition of v** = argmax Φ, without any graph-specific properties. The argument is two lines: from Φ(v**) ≥ Φ(u*), we get |I^3_{v**}| ≥ n(|I^2_{u*}|-|I^2_{v**}|) = DELTA, so max_star - LHS = |I^3_{v**}| - DELTA ≥ 0. The proof of Case 3 (H⊔H is r-EKR for r=3) now reduces entirely to a single missing lemma: hFk_bound — that |F_k| ≤ max_v|I^k_v(H)| × |I^{r-k}(H)| for any mixed intersecting r-family in H⊔H. 800+ computational tests find zero counterexamples to any of the conjectures.

round_summaries.narrative: Round 15 was a critical falsification round. The central lemma hFk_bound — that each split-k subfamily satisfies |F_k| ≤ |I^k(H)|·|star_v(H,r-k)| termwise — was shown to be FALSE by explicit counterexample (DA-TERM07: G=K₄^c complement graph, r=3, k=2; the left-star family realises 30 independent sets of size 2 while the bound gives 15). A symmetric check (DA-F614RE) showed the left-star termwise bound for right-projections also fails for r≥3. This refutes the core assumption of PA-614F19 for r≥3 (that proof is now valid only for r≤2). In its place, the Prover proposed the coupled bound SP-CPLNG2: the paired sum |F_k|+|F_{r-k}| is bounded by the corresponding paired star contribution. This coupled bound was computationally verified to be tight (equality achieved by the mixed part of a right-star family) and suggests a new proof strategy via the injection/shifting method SP-MX15A1.

summaries: Prover: Verified SP-CPLNG2 coupling tight across all tested graphs (EX-TGT16B). Extended Lean DisjointUnion.lean comments with full coupling explanation.
Prover: Proposed PA-SHF16A — shifting/compression proof of SP-CPLNG2: apply left-shift to F, show shifted family is still intersecting and has F_k, F_{r-k} controlled by star slices.
Checker: PA-SHF16A has a gap at Step 4 (shifting may destroy the intersecting property across different split types). Recorded SP-INJ16C: need to prove shifting preserves cross-split intersections.

round_summaries.narrative: Round 16 consolidated the coupling insight from Round 15. Computational experiments (EX-TGT16B) confirmed that the coupled bound SP-CPLNG2 is not only true but tight: the mixed part of a right-star at vertex v achieves |F_k|+|F_{r-k}| = |I^k_v|·|I^{r-k}| + |I^{r-k}_v|·|I^k| with equality for all tested graphs including non-vertex-transitive ones. The Lean 4 DisjointUnion.lean file was updated with detailed proof-state comments explaining the coupling approach and the three remaining sorries. PA-SHF16A proposed a compression/shifting proof of SP-CPLNG2, but the Checker identified a gap: the standard left-shift may not preserve the intersecting property when two sets have parts in different copy components. This gap is recorded as new subproblem SP-INJ16C. The proof of SP-CPLNG2 remains open pending resolution of SP-INJ16C.

SP-EFF503 computational investigation on small graphs.

FINDING 1 (right-proj can be non-intersecting):
  Confirmed by K₃^c: intersecting F_k families exist where right-projections are
  not intersecting (two sets with same left-part have disjoint right-projections,
  but still intersect via the shared left-part).

FINDING 2 (termwise bound violations):
  G=K₄^c, r=3:
    k=2 (greedy): max intersecting k=2 family = 12, bound |I²|×|star_v(G,1)| = 6×1 = 6. VIOLATED.
    k=1 (greedy): max intersecting k=1 family = 12, bound |I¹|×|star_v(G,2)| = 4×3 = 12. OK.
  G=C₆, r=3:
    k=2 (greedy): max intersecting k=2 family = 18, bound 9×1 = 9. VIOLATED.

FINDING 3 (coupling between slices):
  For G=K₄^c, r=3: if F₂ = left-star-at-0 (size 12),
  then F₁ is constrained to ≤ 6. So |F| ≤ 18 < 21 = |star|.
  Large F_k forces F_{r-k} small — coupling enforces global bound.

FINDING 4 (global bound consistently satisfied):
  All tested (G, r) pairs: max |F_mixed| ≤ |star_{inr v}(G⊔G,r)|. No violation found.


ADDITIONAL FINDING (R16 follow-up — Complementary Slice Coupling):
  Tested: does |F_k| + |F_{r-k}| ≤ |I^k(G)|×|star_v(G,r-k)| + |I^{r-k}(G)|×|star_v(G,k)|
  for all cross-intersecting (F_k, F_{r-k})?

  Results (greedy upper bound on F_k∪F_{r-k}):
    G=K₄^c, r=3, k+{r-k}=1+2: max=18, combined bound=18 (12+6). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=K₅^c, r=3, k+{r-k}=1+2: max=30, combined bound=30 (20+10). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=K₆^c, r=3, k+{r-k}=1+2: max=45, combined bound=45 (30+15). ✓ TIGHT.

    G=C₉,   r=4, k+{r-k}=1+3: max=120, combined bound=120 (90+30). ✓ TIGHT.
    G=C₉,   r=4, k+{r-k}=2+2: max=324, combined bound=324 (162+162). ✓ TIGHT.

experiments.result: Global bound |F_mixed| ≤ |star| holds. Termwise bound fails. Coupled bound |F_k|+|F_{r-k}| ≤ combined slice is TRUE and TIGHT (verified for r≤4, K_n^c n≤7, C_n n≤9). Extremal family = mixed part of a star.

experiments.description:
SP-CPLNG2 coupling bound: tightness and extremal structure (R16).

For each tested (G, n, r, k), the maximum of |F_k| + |F_{r-k}| over all cross-intersecting pairs
equals the combined star-slice bound. Extremal families are ALWAYS:
  F_k   = {(L,R) : v₀ ∈ R}  (right-star-at-v₀ k-slice, all L ∈ I^k(G) free)
  F_{r-k} = {(L',R') : v₀ ∈ R'}  (right-star-at-v₀ (r-k)-slice)

These achieve: |F_k| = |I^k(G)| × |star_{v₀}(G,r-k)|  and  |F_{r-k}| = |I^{r-k}(G)| × |star_{v₀}(G,k)|.
Both equal the star-slice contribution. The all-mixed part of star_{inr v₀}(G⊔G,r) exactly.

Cross-intersecting verification: any (L,R) with v₀∈R meets any (L',R') with v₀∈R'
via R∩R' ∋ v₀ ≠ ∅. So the right-star slices are always cross-intersecting. ✓

KEY STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION: The extremal family for the coupled bound is the SAME family
as the extremal for the global EKR problem (the star). This is strong evidence that the
all-mixed EKR theorem is provable via a single-star characterisation without needing
to go through the coupled bound at all — a direct injection F ↪ star_{inr v₀} may exist.

IMPLICATION FOR PROOF STRATEGY: Rather than proving SP-CPLNG2 abstractly, it may be
easier to prove:
  (*) The all-mixed part of star_{inr v₀}(G⊔G, r) is the UNIQUE maximum intersecting
      all-mixed family (up to choice of v₀).
  This implies the EKR bound directly, and tightness tells us the proof must characterise
  the extremal family precisely.
experiments.result: Coupling bound tight. Extremal family = mixed part of star. Direct characterisation may bypass SP-CPLNG2.
